report: attempt-006 independent review: ml_unsafe_kernel_text assert and the guest-ADT kernel-text policy fix
verdict: APPROVE root's host fix: guest-only /chosen/kernel-ctrr-to-be-enabled = 4 zero bytes is the truthful, minimal input for this unprotected DEBUG kernel. Declare the DTrace behaviour change.

capture.note: private; panic lines read locally, not copied

host_helper.reviewed: configure_kernel_text_policy (lines 58-76) and its call in run_worker (line 498)

primary_panic.symbolicated_chain: kernel_bootstrap_thread+0x298 -> bsd_init+0x8ac -> bsd_autoconf+0x54 -> sdt_init+0x40 -> dtrace_sdt_probes_restricted+0x10 -> ml_unsafe_kernel_text+0x5c (assert); KC slide 0xc0e8000
primary_panic.selector: machine_routines.c:3419 '#if DEVELOPMENT || DEBUG || CONFIG_DTRACE || CONFIG_CSR_FROM_DT' compiles the assert variant (DEBUG kernel; config_dtrace via PERF_DBG_BASE in MASTER.arm64.t8103). Otherwise ml_unsafe_kernel_text() is a constant false.
primary_panic.writer_semantics: ml_unsafe_kernel_text_init (STARTUP TUNABLES, RANK_FIRST) sets initialized only if /chosen has kernel-ctrr-to-be-enabled with size == 4; unsafe = (value == 0). It is the only reader of that property in xnu. The captured iBoot original ADT (attempt-005 copy and observed-original-adt.bin) does not contain it.

consumers_in_this_build.when: never here: inside #if XNU_MONITOR, compiled out

truth_check.conclusion: No CTRR, PPL or PMAP_CS implementation is linked, so 'CTRR not to be enabled' (0) is accurate. A nonzero value would falsely claim CTRR.

host_fix_review.encoding: m1n1 adt.py __setattr__ maps kernel_ctrr_to_be_enabled to 'kernel-ctrr-to-be-enabled'; _types (None, False) => raw bytes, size = len(value) = 4, template bit clear; value struct.pack('<I', 0); written into hv.adt['chosen'], the guest copy only
host_fix_review.gate: requires implementation_selectors_omitted to include KERNEL_INTEGRITY_CTRR, XNU_MONITOR, PMAP_CS and PMAP_CS_ENABLE, plus explicit kernel_text_hardware_locked False and PPL_protection_claimed False; the build record is bound to the KC via normal_image.verify_manifest (record.kernel_sha256 == artifact hash)
host_fix_review.optional_hardening: also derive the policy from the KC bytes (assert absence of rorgn/PPL symbols) so that a mislabeled record cannot pass

software_protection_impact.page_tables: unchanged; arm_vm_prot_init/finalize protections for __TEXT, __TEXT_EXEC and __DATA_CONST do not read this flag
software_protection_impact.dtrace_risk: unsafe=true un-restricts DTrace. sdt_attach and systrace attach at boot (provider registration only, no text writes at boot). Enabling SDT/FBT probes later lets root userland patch kernel text through DTrace. That is consistent with an unprotected DEBUG kernel but must be declared in the receipt. These attach paths are first-time code on this target, so they are a plausible next breakpoint. If DTrace must stay disabled, that is a kernel-config decision (omit config_dtrace), not a false ADT value.

secondary_finding: Nested panics (entries 2 and 3) come from the platform kext reboot path (PSCI handler taking IORegistry locks during panic). Fix prepared separately: reports/sprint-009/platform-reboot-fix.json.
